evaluation_philosophy: Descriptive multi-dimensional trade-off matrix. No single scalar score or winner ranking.
dimensions: Cycle A Security Suppression (1:10 duty cycle under R1/R2)
Honest Device Availability (Steps to re-attain ALLOW after false alarm)

B0.name: Memoryless Baseline
B0.strengths: Fastest honest recovery (5 steps); strictly preserves trust convergence.
B0.weaknesses: Vulnerable to single-pulse cyclic exploitation; indefinite period-1 orbit under low noise.
B0.tradeoff_summary: Maximum availability, minimal resistance to periodic gaming.

M1.name: Persistent Evidence Floor
M1.strengths: Directly attacks evidence erasure by retaining latent accumulator memory; bounds accumulator reset.
M1.weaknesses: Does not stop Cycle A if single attack pulse never exceeds gamma=0.335; requires elevated energy to latch.
M1.tradeoff_summary: Highly effective against multi-pulse or high-energy adversaries; neutral against single-pulse low-energy adversaries.

M2.name: History-Dependent Recovery Rate
M2.strengths: Expands required recovery horizon for repeat offenders; reduces sustainable throughput over time.
M2.weaknesses: First incident behaves like B0; requires multiple degradation events before rate suppression takes effect.
M2.tradeoff_summary: Smooth, continuous penalty scaling; honest devices with isolated incidents experience zero long-term penalty.

M3.name: Rehabilitation Hysteresis
M3.strengths: Forces repeat offenders into VERIFY if rest window tau_r < H_req; throttles malicious yield by 50% immediately.
M3.weaknesses: Increases honest device recovery time from 5 steps to H_req=15 steps after a transient false alarm.
M3.tradeoff_summary: Immediate structural barrier against high-frequency cycling; minor temporal friction cost on honest devices.
